title: Postmortem: asymmetric failover cascade during regional autoscale and circuit breaker misconfiguration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-14 18:12 UTC a traffic surge from a partner integration exposed an asymmetric configuration between regions that caused a cascade of failovers and unexpected load shedding. The control plane routing pushed traffic to the secondary region (eu-west-1) while circuit breaker thresholds and per-region concurrency limits there were misaligned with the primary (us-east-1), resulting in prolonged SLO misses and increased 99th-percentile tail latency for generation endpoints. This ticket captures the timeline, root causes, mitigations, and concrete action items.
postmortem_summary: What happened: A partner integration generated a characterized burst of long-sequence generation requests starting 2026-02-14 18:09 UTC. Primary region autoscaling lagged on a small subset of cells; smart routing attempted failover to eu-west-1. Because the CB and concurrency profiles in eu-west-1 were tuned lower and had asymmetric retry/backoff behavior, the region entered partial overload and started shedding load aggressively. That shedding fed back into the control plane routing heuristics which attempted repeated failovers, amplifying the surge. Impact: hosted inference generation SLO (p99 latency target 1500ms) was missed for 28 minutes; ~11% of requests experienced 500/503 or tail latency >5s. Immediate mitigations restored normal traffic after 26 minutes and full SLO recovery after 42 minutes.
root_causes: Asymmetric circuit breaker defaults: eu-west-1 had a lower open threshold and longer cooldown compared to us-east-1 due to an old regional tuning change that was never propagated.

Per-region concurrency mismatch: deployment profiles and cell capacity metadata drift allowed eu-west-1 to accept more concurrent long-sequence allocations than the autoscaler anticipated, exhausting memory and increasing GC pauses.
Routing hysteresis bug: the smart routing policy retried failover rapidly without accounting for region recent failure counts, causing flip-flopping and amplification.
KV cache cold-start penalty: the secondary region did not have warmed KV caches for many active model prefixes causing amplified per-request compute and elevated tail latency.
Insufficient runbook coverage: the on-call runbook lacked a clear playbook for simultaneous autoscale lag + failover oscillation, leading to manual mitigation delays.
timeline: 2026-02-14 18:09 UTC - Large burst of long-sequence generation requests detected (partner integration traffic spike).

2026-02-14 18:12 UTC - Primary cells in us-east-1 observed elevated p99; autoscaler reacted but new pods not fully provisioned yet. Control plane routed ~30% of traffic to eu-west-1 per failover policy.
2026-02-14 18:15 UTC - eu-west-1 CBs tripped due to lower thresholds; region began shedding and returning 503s for a subset of routes. On-call paged.
2026-02-14 18:22 UTC - Routing oscillation observed: repeated failover attempts between regions increased tail latency globally.
2026-02-14 18:35 UTC - Emergency mitigation: engineers applied temporary routing quiesce to stop cross-region failovers and increased eu-west-1 concurrency caps. Immediate error rate dropped.
2026-02-14 18:41 UTC - Manual cache-warmup job triggered and KV prefix prefetch started for high-volume models in eu-west-1.
2026-02-14 18:50 UTC - Traffic normalized; final SLO recovery verified at 19:00 UTC after continued monitoring.
2026-02-15 - Post-incident analysis started; metrics exported and preliminary RCA drafted by SRE and Runtime teams.
metrics: Generation p99 latency target: 1500ms; observed peak p99: 8200ms
Error rate (5xx) baseline: 0.2%; peak during incident: 11.3%
Duration of primary SLO miss window: 28 minutes (18:12-18:40 UTC)
Fraction of requests affected: approximately 11% of partner integration requests during spike
Autoscaler scale up lag: median provision time for new capacity was 3.8 minutes vs expected 90s
mitigations: Immediate: quiesced cross-region failovers for affected model routes to prevent oscillation.
Immediate: temporarily increased eu-west-1 concurrency caps and shortened CB cooldown to allow graceful recovery.
Short-term: triggered KV cache prefetch for top 20 model prefixes used by the partner integration in eu-west-1.
Monitoring: added an alert for cross-region failover rate > 5% over 2m to catch oscillation early.
action_items: Marco Ruiz - Audit and unify circuit breaker defaults across regions; deploy symmetric CB policy and add a config validation that blocks asymmetric defaults - due 2026-03-03

SRE Team (owner: Priya Menon) - Implement routing hysteresis: require >=30s steady failure rate before triggering region failover and add exponential backoff between failover attempts - due 2026-03-10
Runtime Team (owner: David Kim) - Add a KV cache warmup step to autoscale flow so new cells prefetch hot prefixes before accepting traffic - due 2026-03-17
Autoscaler Team (owner: Elena Garcia) - Reduce median provision time to <=90s by benchmarking image startup and optimizing init containers; produce performance report - due 2026-04-01
SRE/Oncall Docs (owner: Oliver Chen) - Update runbook to include combined autoscale+failover playbook and checklist; include decision tree and rollback commands - due 2026-02-28
Observability (owner: Sana Malik) - Add dashboard panels showing per-region CB open counts, per-route failover counts, and a failover-oscillation small-multiples view - due 2026-03-05
Product (owner: Maya Thompson) - Communicate incident summary and preventive measures to affected partner and coordinate SLA/credits if requested - due 2026-02-21
